title: Remember the Night God Freed You

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Observe the month of Aviv and celebrate the Passover of the Lord your God, because in the month of Aviv he brought you out of Egypt by night. - Deut 16:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the people settled into the land, God gave them a calendar of remembering. The very first appointment was the Passover, tied to the month of Aviv, the exact time God had carried them out of Egypt by night. God did not want them to forget the night everything changed, the night the blood on the doorframe stood between them and death.

Notice how personal God is here. He does not say "when Israel escaped," but "he brought you out." Deliverance was His work from beginning to end. Left to themselves, they could never have broken Pharaoh's grip.

You and I need this same rhythm of remembering. It is so easy to move on quickly and forget the rescue that made everything else possible. The Passover pointed forward to Christ, our Passover Lamb, whose blood was shed so that judgment would pass over us (1 Cor 5:7). When you take the Lord's Supper, you are doing exactly what Israel did here, deliberately remembering the night your freedom was purchased. Do not rush past that memory. Let it steady you when life feels uncertain.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does it mean to you that God says "he brought you out"?
2. How often do you deliberately remember your rescue in Christ?
3. What helps you keep the cross fresh in your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for rescuing me when I could not save myself. Keep the memory of Christ my Passover Lamb ever fresh in my heart. Amen.
